highlights.heading: Explore Banff’s must-see lakes and canyons with us!
paragraphs: This top-rated shared tour takes you to nine iconic locations, including Lake Louise, Moraine Lake, Bow Lake, Peyto Lake, and Johnston Canyon. Travel in comfort with hotel pickup, a friendly local guide, and plenty of time for photos at each stop. From turquoise lakes and waterfalls to scenic mountain views, you’ll experience the true beauty of the Canadian Rockies — all in a single, adventure-filled day. Perfect for first-time visitors and budget-savvy travelers who want to see the most of Banff in one day.

highlights.heading: What You’ll See on This Tour
paragraphs:
Moraine Lake (June–October): Nestled in the Valley of the Ten Peaks, Moraine Lake glows with glacial blue hues. Spend time walking along the shoreline or climbing the rock pile for that iconic Canadian Rockies photo.
Winter Alternate:Visit Emerald Lake and Natural Bridge in Yoho National Park equally stunning with frozen cascades and emerald reflections.
Lake Louise: Admire the world-famous turquoise waters backed by Victoria Glacier. Stroll the lakeshore or snap postcard views from the Fairmont Chateau terrace.
Bow Lake & Crowfoot Glacier: Along the Icefields Parkway, Bow Lake offers mirror-like reflections of the Wapta Icefield. Just beyond, Crowfoot Glacier — named for its claw-like shape — gives a striking glimpse into Banff’s icy heart.
Peyto Lake Viewpoint: This wolf-shaped lake is one of the most photographed spots in the Rockies. Walk a short paved trail to the overlook and marvel at its surreal blue color.
Johnston Canyon: Walk the scenic catwalks to the Lower Falls, where water tumbles through narrow limestone walls. A short, easy hike with incredible photo opportunities.
Castle Mountain: Enjoy a scenic drive-by view of the impressive Castle Mountain rising above the surrounding valley, with its dramatic peaks and beautiful Rocky Mountain scenery.
Mount Norquay Lookout: End the day with a sweeping view over Banff town and Bow Valley — a peaceful finale before your return.

faqs.question: How long is the Banff Standard Shared Tour?
faqs.answer: The full tour lasts between 9 and 11 hours , depending on weather and road conditions. Pickup is between 7:00 and 8:00 AM from your Banff or Canmore accommodation, and drop-off is typically around 5:00–7:00 PM .

faqs.question: What sights are included in the Banff Standard Tour?
faqs.answer: This tour covers all the must-see spots in Banff National Park: Lake Louise, Moraine Lake (summer only), Bow Lake, Peyto Lake, Crowfoot Glacier, Johnston Canyon, Morant’s Curve, Castle Mountain Lookout, and Mount Norquay Viewpoint. During winter, Emerald Lake and Natural Bridge in Yoho National Park replace Moraine Lake.

faqs.question: Is lunch included in the price?
faqs.answer: Lunch is not included , but your guide will schedule a stop in Lake Louise Village where you can choose from a variety of restaurants and cafés. A complimentary water bottle is provided for every guest.

faqs.question: Do you offer doorstep pickup and drop off?
faqs.answer: We offer doorstep pickups in Banff and Canmore. If your location is outside the pickup area, we’ll confirm a nearby meeting point before your travel date, easy and stress-free.

faqs.question: How many people are in each group?
faqs.answer: To keep the experience personal and comfortable, we limit each vehicle to a maximum of 12 guests . This allows for more flexible photo stops, better interaction with your guide, and an overall smoother journey.

faqs.question: Is this tour suitable for families and seniors?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. The Banff Standard Shared Tour is designed for all ages 2 and above. The walking sections are light to moderate, and your guide will tailor stops to suit everyone’s comfort level.

faqs.question: When is the best time to visit Moraine Lake?
faqs.answer: Moraine Lake is open June 1 – October 10 , depending on road and weather conditions. If you’re visiting outside this period, don’t worry - you’ll visit Emerald Lake and Natural Bridge instead, which are equally spectacular in winter.

faqs.question: What should I bring?
faqs.answer: Wear comfortable walking shoes and dress in layers. Mountain weather can change quickly. Bring a jacket, camera, sunscreen, and a refillable water bottle.

faqs.question: How do I book and pay?
faqs.answer: You can easily book online through Vista Chase or by contacting us directly at support@vistachase.com. Payment is secure and confirmed instantly. Your guide will reach out the day before your tour with final pickup details.

faqs.question: What is your cancellation policy?
faqs.answer: Cancel at least 72 hours before your tour for a full refund (groups of 1–6). For groups of 7 or more, the 20% deposit is non-refundable and the rest is refunded. Cancellations within 72 hours aren't refunded.

From sparkling waterfalls to panoramic viewpoints, the Heart of Banff Shared Tour reveals the magic that made Banff National Park world-famous. highlights.heading: Experience the Soul of the Canadian Rockies
paragraphs:
Discover why Banff is called the heart of the Rockies on this full-day Banff shared tour that blends mountain views, turquoise lakes, and fascinating stories from your local guide. Perfect for first-time visitors, families, couples, and solo travelers, this small-group adventure offers the perfect mix of famous landmarks and hidden gems around Banff town — without the stress of driving or parking.
With doorstep pickup from Banff or Canmore, a friendly guide, and comfortable SUV or van transport, this Banff day trip is the most effortless way to capture Banff’s beauty and spirit — all starting from just CAD $149.

highlights.heading: What You’ll See on This Tour
paragraphs:
Bow Falls — Banff’s Roaring Gateway
Start your day at Bow Falls, where glacier-fed waters crash into the Bow River below the historic Fairmont Banff Springs. The mist and roar of the falls make it one of Banff’s most iconic photo spots — especially in the morning light.
Banff Gondola — Panoramic Peaks from Sulphur Mountain
Ride the Banff Gondola to the summit of Sulphur Mountain for a breathtaking 360° view of six mountain ranges. From the top, follow the boardwalk to Sanson’s Peak or enjoy lunch at Sky Bistro.
Tunnel Mountain — The Sleeping Buffalo
Named for its resemblance to a resting buffalo, Tunnel Mountain offers a panoramic view of Banff town below. Your guide shares stories of its significance in local Indigenous culture and early Canadian mountaineering.
Surprise Corner — The Fairmont Viewpoint
A classic Banff sightseeing tour stop! This viewpoint reveals the majestic Fairmont Banff Springs Hotel nestled amid forest and mountain backdrops — a must for photography lovers.
Lake Minnewanka — Banff’s Blue Gem
Translated from Stoney Nakoda as “Lake of the Spirits,” Lake Minnewanka is the largest lake in Banff National Park. It’s a peaceful place to spot wildlife, admire turquoise waters, and enjoy scenic walks along the shoreline.
Two Jack Lake & Johnson Lake — Peaceful Reflections
These sister lakes near Lake Minnewanka are beloved for their calm reflections and easy lakeside trails. Perfect for serene photography stops or a short stroll with panoramic mountain views.
Mount Norquay Lookout — Banff’s Skyline View
Climb up to Mount Norquay Lookout for one of the best views of Banff town, framed by Cascade Mountain. This stop offers a chance to see elk grazing and, in winter, the slopes dotted with skiers.
Hoodoos Lookout — Nature’s Sandstone Spires
Finish the scenic loop with a stop at Hoodoos Lookout, where wind and water sculpted towering sandstone pillars. Overlooking the Bow Valley, it’s a natural wonder that makes a perfect finale to your Banff adventure.

highlights.heading: Banff & Yoho National Parks — Two Wonders, One Epic Day
paragraphs:
See the most breathtaking sights of Banff and Yoho National Parks on this all-inclusive shared day tour designed for travelers who want to experience the very best of the Canadian Rockies without driving or planning.
Perfect for first-time visitors, couples, families, and solo explorers, this 9–11 hour guided adventure combines Banff’s turquoise lakes and Yoho’s dramatic waterfalls into a single, unforgettable journey.
With small groups (max 12 guests), doorstep pickup from Banff or Canmore, and comfortable seating in premium sprinter vans, this is the easiest and most affordable Banff tour to capture world-famous scenery in one day — all starting from just CAD $199.

highlights.heading: What You’ll See on This Tour
paragraphs:
Lake Louise — The Jewel of Banff
Nestled beneath the majestic Victoria Glacier, Lake Louise is one of the most photographed lakes in the world. Its turquoise color shifts with the light, framed by snow-capped peaks. Stroll along the lakeshore, enjoy peaceful mountain air, and capture postcard-perfect views — a highlight of every Banff sightseeing tour.
Moraine Lake (Summer) / Johnston Canyon (Winter)
When open from June to mid-October, Moraine Lake shines with surreal blue waters surrounded by the Ten Peaks. Walk up the Rockpile Trail for sweeping panoramas — it’s pure Canadian magic.
In winter, Johnston Canyon offers an equally spectacular scene, with frozen waterfalls and icy trails that sparkle in the morning sun.
Takakkaw Falls — Yoho’s Mighty Cascade
Standing at over 373 meters, Takakkaw Falls is one of Canada’s tallest and most powerful waterfalls. Watch as meltwater plunges from Daly Glacier in Yoho National Park. This natural wonder translates to “magnificent” in Cree — and it truly is.
Emerald Lake — A Tranquil Mirror of the Mountains
The centerpiece of Yoho, Emerald Lake lives up to its name with deep green hues caused by glacier silt. It’s surrounded by lush forests and limestone peaks — perfect for photos or a short lakeside stroll. No Banff Yoho day trip is complete without it.
Natural Bridge — Yoho’s Sculpted Wonder
Witness nature’s craftsmanship at the Natural Bridge, where the Kicking Horse River carved a limestone arch over centuries. It’s a powerful example of water meeting rock — and a favorite stop on our Banff to Yoho day trip.
Bow Lake & Peyto Lake — Glacier Reflections on the Parkway
Travel along the legendary Icefields Parkway, one of the most scenic drives in the world. Stop at Bow Lake and Peyto Lake, where the glacier-fed waters glimmer in brilliant shades of blue. At Peyto Lake Lookout, the view resembles a wolf’s head — a must-see for photographers.
Crowfoot Glacier Lookout — A Glimpse into the Ice Age
Named for its three-pronged glacier (once shaped like a crow’s foot), this viewpoint offers insight into the Rockies’ ancient past. It’s a reminder of how powerful nature’s slow artistry can be.

highlights.heading: Glaciers, Waterfalls & Wildlife in One Epic Day
paragraphs: Experience one of the world’s most spectacular drives on this Icefields Parkway & Jasper shared tour — a breathtaking 10–12 hour journey through the heart of the Canadian Rockies.Perfect for first-time travelers, couples, families, and small groups, this guided adventure connects Banff National Park and Jasper National Park along the legendary Icefields Parkway — a route lined with turquoise lakes, ancient glaciers, and thundering waterfalls.

highlights.heading: What You’ll See on This Tour
paragraphs:
Bow Lake: Gateway to the Icefields
Fed by Bow Glacier, this turquoise lake mirrors the surrounding Wapta Icefield peaks. It’s one of the first major stops on your Icefields Parkway day trip, offering panoramic views and tranquil walking paths.
Peyto Lake: The Wolf’s Head Jewel
At 1,860 meters above sea level, Peyto Lake is famous for its shape and bright glacier-fed color. It’s a must-see for any Canadian Rockies guided tour, especially from the upper viewing deck where the valley opens below.
Crowfoot Glacier Lookout: Frozen in Time
Once shaped like a crow’s foot, this glacier is a living reminder of the Rockies’ changing climate. Your guide explains its retreat and importance in feeding Bow Lake and the Bow River system.
Weeping Wall & Waterfowl Lake: Nature’s Artistry
Marvel at Weeping Wall, a towering cliff face where dozens of streams trickle down like silver tears. Nearby, Waterfowl Lake sparkles in deep shades of blue-green — another stunning photo opportunity.
Athabasca Glacier: Walk Among Ancient Ice
The star of the Columbia Icefield tour, this massive glacier flows down from the Columbia Icefield — one of the largest accumulations of ice south of the Arctic Circle.
You can choose to join the optional Ice Explorer bus tour for an up-close experience on the glacier (tickets not included).
Columbia Icefield Skywalk: Adventure on the Edge
Feel the thrill of walking on a glass-floored platform suspended 280 meters above the Sunwapta Valley. The Columbia Icefield Skywalk offers jaw-dropping views of glaciers, cliffs, and waterfalls. (Optional add-on; entry not included.)
Sunwapta Falls: Thundering Through the Canyon
Just south of Jasper, Sunwapta Falls cascades through a narrow limestone canyon. It’s particularly impressive during spring melt, when glacial runoff surges through the valley.
Athabasca Falls: Jasper’s Powerhouse
Known for its raw power, Athabasca Falls carves through ancient rock at a roaring pace. Even in mid-summer, the icy blue waters remind travelers of the Rockies’ glacial origins.
Tangle Falls: Layers of Ice and Mist
One of the most photographed roadside waterfalls in Jasper National Park, Tangle Falls creates a mesmerizing curtain of water — a fitting finale to your Banff Jasper day trip.

highlights.heading: Discover Frozen Wonders of Banff, Lake Louise & Abraham Lake
paragraphs:
Experience the Canadian Rockies transformed into a winter wonderland on this one-of-a-kind Winter Special Tour— a full-day shared journey through frozen lakes, glittering glaciers, and breathtaking mountain scenery.
Perfect for winter travelers, couples, families, and photographers, this tour combines the beauty of Banff, Lake Louise, and Abraham Lake in a single unforgettable day.
Travel comfortably in a heated SUV or van, with a maximum of 12 guests for a relaxed, friendly experience. From CAD $199, this is your chance to capture the Rockies’ rarest winter sights — including the world-famous ice bubbles of Abraham Lake.

highlights.heading: What You’ll See on This Tour
paragraphs:
Lake Louise: The Icon in Ice
Start your day at Lake Louise, where the emerald waters of summer turn into a frozen mirror framed by towering peaks. Watch skaters glide across the lake, admire the Fairmont Château’s ice sculptures, or simply soak in the serenity — it’s the picture-perfect start to your Lake Louise winter tour.
Abraham Lake: Alberta’s Ice Bubble Wonder
The star of your journey, Abraham Lake is world-famous for its frozen methane bubbles trapped beneath layers of transparent ice. Your guide will lead you safely onto the ice using provided ice cleats, helping you capture the best photos of this rare natural phenomenon. This stop is the highlight of any Abraham Lake ice bubbles tour and a dream for photographers.
Howse Pass Viewpoint: Gateway to the Icefields
At Howse Pass Viewpoint, admire sweeping views of the Icefields Parkway and its snow-covered valleys. It’s a quiet, less-visited gem offering incredible panoramas and a true sense of wilderness in the heart of the Rockies.
Peyto Lake: The Frozen Wolf’s Head
Known for its unique shape, Peyto Lake becomes a frozen landscape of white and blue hues during winter. From the lookout, enjoy an unmatched view of Banff’s alpine beauty — a must-see stop for your Canadian Rockies winter tour.
Bow Lake: Tranquil Reflections Beneath Snowy Peaks
Nestled along the Icefields Parkway, Bow Lake sits peacefully beneath Crowfoot Mountain. In winter, the frozen surface reflects the soft light of the season, making it a peaceful stop for photos or quiet reflection.
Crowfoot Glacier Lookout: Frozen in Time
Named for its three-pronged glacier (once shaped like a crow’s foot), this lookout offers a glimpse into Banff’s glacial history. On clear winter days, you’ll see deep crevasses and hanging ice shimmering in the sunlight — a truly iconic Banff winter sight.
Johnston Canyon: Banff’s Hidden Waterfall Paradise (Optional, Depending on available Daylight)
In winter, Johnston Canyon transforms into a magical world of ice and snow, where frozen waterfalls hang like crystal curtains from towering canyon walls. Walk safely along the maintained catwalks as your guide leads you to the Lower and Upper Falls, both spectacularly encased in shimmering blue ice. The sound of rushing water beneath the frozen surface adds to the enchantment.

sections.heading: Discover Frozen Wonders of Banff, Lake Louise & Abraham Lake
body:
Experience the Canadian Rockies transformed into a winter wonderland on this one-of-a-kind Winter Special Tour— a full-day shared journey through frozen lakes, glittering glaciers, and breathtaking mountain scenery.
Perfect for winter travelers, couples, families, and photographers, this tour combines the beauty of Banff, Lake Louise, and Abraham Lake in a single unforgettable day.
Travel comfortably in a heated SUV or van, with a maximum of 12 guests for a relaxed, friendly experience. From CAD $199, this is your chance to capture the Rockies’ rarest winter sights — including the world-famous ice bubbles of Abraham Lake.

sections.heading: What You’ll See on This Tour

stops.name: Lake Louise: The Icon in Ice
stops.text: Start your day at Lake Louise, where the emerald waters of summer turn into a frozen mirror framed by towering peaks. Watch skaters glide across the lake, admire the Fairmont Château’s ice sculptures, or simply soak in the serenity — it’s the picture-perfect start to your Lake Louise winter tour.

stops.name: Abraham Lake: Alberta’s Ice Bubble Wonder
stops.text: The star of your journey, Abraham Lake is world-famous for its frozen methane bubbles trapped beneath layers of transparent ice. Your guide will lead you safely onto the ice using provided ice cleats, helping you capture the best photos of this rare natural phenomenon. This stop is the highlight of any Abraham Lake ice bubbles tour and a dream for photographers.

stops.name: Howse Pass Viewpoint: Gateway to the Icefields
stops.text: At Howse Pass Viewpoint, admire sweeping views of the Icefields Parkway and its snow-covered valleys. It’s a quiet, less-visited gem offering incredible panoramas and a true sense of wilderness in the heart of the Rockies.

stops.name: Peyto Lake: The Frozen Wolf’s Head
stops.text: Known for its unique shape, Peyto Lake becomes a frozen landscape of white and blue hues during winter. From the lookout, enjoy an unmatched view of Banff’s alpine beauty — a must-see stop for your Canadian Rockies winter tour.

stops.name: Bow Lake: Tranquil Reflections Beneath Snowy Peaks
stops.text: Nestled along the Icefields Parkway, Bow Lake sits peacefully beneath Crowfoot Mountain. In winter, the frozen surface reflects the soft light of the season, making it a peaceful stop for photos or quiet reflection.

stops.name: Crowfoot Glacier Lookout: Frozen in Time

Walk safely along the maintained catwalks as your guide leads you to the Lower and Upper Falls, both spectacularly encased in shimmering blue ice. faqs.question: Is a private tour in Banff worth it?
faqs.answer: Yes — private tours offer unmatched flexibility, comfort, and a more personalized experience. You avoid the rigidity of large group schedules, linger where you want, skip what doesn’t interest you, and enjoy deeper engagement with your guide.

faqs.question: Can you visit Moraine Lake on a private tour?
faqs.answer: Although access is restricted to private vehicles during peak season, many operators (including us) use our commercial shuttles. Contact us in advance for private access to Moraine Lake if you have booked our 6 Passanger SUV option (June–October). If customer booked a 12 Passenger Van option Moraine lake private entry is included in the price.

faqs.question: How long is our private tour of Banff?
faqs.answer: Most full-day private tours run 9 to 11 hours , depending on your starting point and how many stops you want to make.

faqs.question: What is included in a Banff private tour?
faqs.answer: Typical inclusions are: private vehicle + driver/guide, hotel pickup/dropoff, park fees, flexible itinerary, bottled water, and seasonal access to special areas like Moraine Lake. Optional upgrades (like sunrise access or a more luxurious vehicle) may cost extra.

faqs.question: Can you customize stops on a private Banff tour?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. One of the key perks of a private tour is the flexibility to add, skip, or lengthen stops according to your interests — whether that’s photography, hiking, wildlife, or relaxing by the lake.

faqs.question: What is the best time to visit Moraine Lake?
faqs.answer: Early morning (sunrise) tends to offer the most magical light, fewer crowds, and calm water reflections. Also, the window of accessibility is limited — generally June through early October — depending on snow melt and road conditions.

faqs.question: How many people can join a private tour?
faqs.answer: Private tours usually accommodate small groups — typically up to 6 people — so you all travel together without sharing your guide or vehicle with strangers.

faqs.question: Are meals included in a private tour?
faqs.answer: Meals are usually not included , though your guide can recommend great picnic spots or restaurants. Some premium tours may offer lunch as an optional add-on.

faqs.question: What happens if the weather is bad?
faqs.answer: Tours run in all weather. Guides adapt in real time — adjusting the route, timing, or even swapping out stops — to still deliver a safe, enjoyable, and memorable experience.

faqs.question: How do private tours avoid the crowds?
faqs.answer: Private tours use insider knowledge of timing and less-traveled routes. Also, with commercial access or permits (for places like Moraine Lake), they can bypass the constraints normal vehicles face.

highlights.heading: What You’ll See on This Tour
paragraphs:
Bow Lake
One of Banff’s most photogenic stops, Bow Lake mirrors Crowfoot Mountain and Bow Glacier in its still turquoise waters. It’s an ideal first stop for reflection shots and a peaceful morning stroll.
Peyto Lake
Shaped like a wolf’s head, Peyto Lake is an elevated viewpoint with breathtaking color intensity, especially under clear skies. Your guide will time the visit for the best light.
Crowfoot Glacier
Once resembling a three-toed crow’s foot, this glacier tells a visual story of time and climate change. It’s an easy roadside stop with sweeping mountain views.
Big Bend Viewpoint
One of the Parkway’s most iconic curves, offering panoramic vistas of endless valleys and snow-capped summits — a must for panoramic photos.
Waterfowl Lake & Weeping Wall
Two hidden gems along the route: turquoise lakes framed by alpine peaks and waterfalls streaming down sheer cliffs — natural wonders that many large tour buses skip.
Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre (Lunch Stop)
Pause for lunch with glacier views. Visit the interpretive centre, learn about the Icefields, and prepare for the highlight of the day — the Athabasca Glacier and Skywalk.
Athabasca Glacier (Optional Ice Explorer Ride)
Hop aboard a Glacier Bus for a once-in-a-lifetime ride onto the ice itself. Your guide will assist with tickets and timing so you enjoy the experience stress-free.
Skywalk
Walk on a glass platform suspended above a dramatic canyon, offering jaw-dropping views of the Sunwapta Valley below.
Tangle Falls
A scenic, easily accessible cascade that tumbles gracefully along the cliffs — a perfect short stop for photos.
Sunwapta Falls & Athabasca Falls
Powerful waterfalls surrounded by jagged canyons and misty spray — a fitting finale before entering Jasper National Park.
At day’s end, choose to return to Banff or Lake Louise or stay overnight in Jasper for a relaxed evening.

highlights.heading: What You Can See on This Tour

Jasper National Park Highlights
Maligne Lake
A stunning alpine lake famous for its deep blue color and reflection of the surrounding peaks. The perfect starting point for photography and relaxation.
Spirit Island (Cruise Ticket Extra)
Accessible only by boat, Spirit Island is a Canadian icon often featured in travel magazines. The Maligne Lake Cruiseoffers unforgettable views and photo opportunities.
Medicine Lake (Ghost Lake)
Known for its disappearing waters caused by underground drainage. Wildlife sightings — especially elk and bears — are common in this valley.
Maligne Canyon
One of the deepest limestone canyons in the Rockies. Walk along suspended bridges for breathtaking views of waterfalls crashing below.
Pyramid Lake
A serene spot near Jasper town, famous for its calm waters, mountain reflections, and easy access to Pyramid Island.
Athabasca Falls
Feel the power of water as it carves through ancient rock — a short, dramatic stop that’s among Jasper’s most photographed locations.
Sunwapta Falls
Another spectacular waterfall along Icefields Parkway, plunging into a deep canyon framed by forest and mountain peaks.
Cavell Lake (Seasonal: June–October)
A quiet alpine lake surrounded by wildflowers and hanging glaciers, accessible only in summer.
Skywalk (Seasonal: Ticket Extra)
Step out onto a glass platform 918 feet above the valley floor for an adrenaline-filled view of glaciers and cliffs.
Athabasca Glacier (Bus Ride Extra)
Take a Glacier Bus ride for an unforgettable walk on ancient ice, or enjoy a short hike near Sunwapta Lake for panoramic views.
Bow Lake

faqs.question: How does the customizable Jasper private tour work?
faqs.answer: You choose 6 destinations from our curated list of Jasper and Icefields Parkway highlights. Your private guide plans the best route for the day, adapting stops based on weather, timing, and your preferences.

faqs.question: Can we include both Jasper and Icefields Parkway stops?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. You can combine locations from Jasper National Park and the Icefields Parkway ; your guide balances travel time to create a full yet relaxing day.

faqs.question: How do you get to Spirit Island in Jasper?
faqs.answer: Spirit Island can only be reached by boat. The Maligne Lake Cruise departs regularly from Maligne Lake and includes commentary about the region’s geology and wildlife.

faqs.question: Is the Spirit Island cruise included in Jasper private tours?
faqs.answer: The Spirit Island Cruise is an optional add-on — it’s not automatically included in private tours. Tickets can be arranged through your guide in advance or purchased directly at Maligne Lake.

faqs.question: How long is the Spirit Island boat cruise?
faqs.answer: The cruise lasts about 90 minutes round-trip , with multiple departures daily (usually from mid-June to early October).

faqs.question: Can you walk on Spirit Island?
faqs.answer: No, Spirit Island itself is protected and off-limits to foot traffic. The cruise docks nearby at a viewing platform where you can take stunning photos and enjoy the view.

faqs.question: Do Jasper private tours include wildlife viewing?
faqs.answer: Yes, wildlife sightings are common along the Icefields Parkway and around Jasper. Your guide will make safe stops when possible for photos of elk, bears, mountain goats, or deer.

faqs.question: Where do we stop for lunch?
faqs.answer: Lunch is usually enjoyed at either the Columbia Icefield Discovery Centre or in Jasper town , depending on your itinerary. Your guide will suggest the best local spots for great food and mountain views.

faqs.question: Are Cavell Lake and Skywalk open all year?
faqs.answer: No, Cavell Lake is open from June to October (weather-dependent), and the Skywalk operates seasonally from May to October.

faqs.question: Is the Glacier Bus ride included?
faqs.answer: It’s an optional upgrade at Athabasca Glacier . Guests can either join the Glacier Bus experience (ticket required) or take a short self-guided hike near Sunwapta Lake for glacier views.

faqs.question: Is the Lowest Price Guarantee included?
faqs.answer: Always. If you find the same Jasper private itinerary at a lower verified price, Vista Chase will match it, guaranteed.

sections.heading: What Your Multi-Day Trip Can Include
body:
Stunning Lakes:
Lake Louise, Moraine Lake, Peyto Lake, Emerald Lake, Bow Lake, Two Jack Lake.
Waterfalls & Canyons:
Takakkaw Falls, Sunwapta Falls, Athabasca Falls, Johnston Canyon, Marble Canyon.
Mountain & Parkway Highlights:
Icefields Parkway, Crowfoot Glacier, Mistaya Canyon, Athabasca Glacier (optional ice explorer bus).
Special Experiences:
Wildlife viewing, Sunset lookouts & stargazing, Boat cruises (Spirit Island), Snowshoeing & short hikes, Columbia Icefield Skywalk

stops.name: 2–3 Days
stops.text: A perfect introduction to the Rockies. Visit iconic lakes, major viewpoints, and essential stops in Banff, Yoho, or Jasper. Ideal for travelers with a short stay who want to see the biggest highlights without rushing.

stops.name: 4–5 Days
stops.text: More time means more depth. Explore Banff’s top lakes, Yoho’s waterfalls, and Jasper’s canyons with time for optional experiences like the Glacier Adventure, Skywalk, and Spirit Island cruise.

stops.name: 6–7 Days
stops.text: A complete Canadian Rockies journey. Cover multiple national parks, enjoy sunrise visits, slow travel days, and hidden gems along the Icefields Parkway. Perfect for families and travelers wanting a rich, immersive experience.

sections.heading: Seasonal Notes
items: Moraine Lake: Open from June to mid‑October only.
Takakkaw Falls : Summer access only.
Winter Activities: Snowshoeing, frozen canyon walks, wildlife spotting.
Spring & Fall : Ideal for fewer crowds and golden light.
Summer: Best for long days, open roads, and boat/cruise activities.

faqs.question: Can we choose our own locations?
faqs.answer: Yes — every day is planned around your choices.

faqs.question: Is it suitable for families and seniors?
